newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rain again in France but sunshine to make comeback.
newsitem.headline: Rain again in France but sunshine to make comeback.

text.p: Rain fell over much of northeastern France again on Tuesday but forecasters predicted dry, sunny weather would return on Wednesday.

Showers were expected during the day from the Alsace region south to the Alps, marking the fifth day of rain in France after three months of drought which have dashed farmers expectations and driven up prices.
Central France would see light showers interrupted by periods of sunshine in the late afternoon, while the Picardie region north of Paris would see heavier rainfalls, Meteo France said.
Elsewhere, there would be sunshine, particularly along the Mediterranean coast and western France, the forecasters said.
For Wednesday, sunshine was expected to make a comeback across France apart from the Mediterranean island of Corsica and the mountainous southeast.
The clear weather was likely to persist through Saturday, Meteo France forecaster Dominique Escale said.
A string of rainy days has given crops a good watering but has not been heavy enough to replenish depleted water tables, Escale said.
"The rain has brought a bit of relief to the countryside, decreasing the risk of forest fires, but it has not been enough" to end the dry spell, she said.

On Monday eight to 13 mm of rain fell over the Pyrenees in southern France, 12 mm doused central France, 2 mm sprinkled the Paris area and three to seven mm fell in the northeast, according to Meteo France figures.
